one_month_reasoning: Eaton has not announced a Q3 date. EDGAR shows no new 8-K since the Jul 31 Q2 filing, re-checked Sep 30. Aggregators estimate Nov 3, but Eaton reported Q3 on Oct 31 in 2023 and 2024, so I put ~25-30% odds on a print by Oct 30. At the Sep 16 Laguna conference management said Q3 was 'very strong' and tracking toward the high end of the $3.46-3.56 guide. An in-window print would therefore lean slightly positive, but a 170bp margin step-up still has to show up, so mainly it adds variance. The other in-window events are two-sided. The Oct 27-28 FOMC comes after the Sep 17 hike to a 4.00% upper bound, with the 10-year at 5.24% on Sep 28 (FRED); a second hike would hit a 27x-multiple stock. Hyperscaler Q3 capex calls and VRT, GEV and Schneider Q3 reports in late October are the other two. The stock is 10% below its $478 high after the mid-September AI-slowdown dip and the post-Laguna rebound, which gives no clean momentum signal. I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$433 (tiny drift) with ~11% monthly vol (39%/3.5). The downside is a touch wider than the upside because of the rate-hike risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (65%) and FCF yield (35%), both on a pro-forma ex-Mobility basis. P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of ~$16.95 x 25.5x = $432. FCF yield: NTM FCF ~$5.0B / ~380.5M shares = $13.1/share at a 3.1% yield = $424. Blended ≈ $430.

inputs_detail.derivation: +17% on the $13.50 midpoint, which matches the $15.5-15.8 consensus (src 9). Support: backlog +33% in EA, +103% in EG and +28% in Aero (src 1, 4), and price/cost turning into a 2027 tailwind (src 5).

Mobility segment profit is ~$109M/qtr (src 1), so ~$436M/yr, or ~$360M after tax at ~17%. Against that: ~$40M interest saved on the $1.1B cash, which Eaton says goes 'including repayment of outstanding indebtedness' (src 3, 13), at ~4.5% pre-tax. Shares fall from 389.5M to ~380.5M. Result: (15.80 x 389.5M - 360M + 40M) / 380.5M = $15.33, so ~$15.30. I accept the supervisor's ~$0.5 correction over my round-1 $0.2. Stranded corporate cost is a small further risk I do not model.
$15.80 less $0.50 of RMT dilution. Close is expected in Q1 2027, so reported 2027 will carry ~1 quarter of Mobility. For the NTM multiple at the horizon, full pro forma is the right base.

+14.4%, slightly above round 1 because the remaining mix is higher-growth. Management says the deal is 'immediately accretive to organic growth and margins' (src 3). ~80% of the 307 GW US data-center backlog converts in 2028+ (src 6). The 32% EA margin target is for 2030 (src 6).

ETN trades at ~27.5x 2027 consensus and ~32x 2026 guidance (src 1, 9, 10). In round 1 I used 26x and ignored rates. At 25.5x the earnings yield is 3.9%, about 130bp below a 5.24% 10-year (src 14). A mid-teens EPS CAGR justifies that, but the rate backdrop argues for a further ~0.5-turn de-rating and against any re-rating. The ex-Mobility mix, with higher growth and margins, partly offsets, so I cut only 0.5 turns.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Sep-2027 ~$5.0B ex-Mobility; ~380.5M shares post split-off; 3.1% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 is ~$4.0B (H1 $1.19B plus a seasonally strong H2). It grows ~18-20%/yr with EPS and Boyd, less ~$0.35-0.4B of Mobility FCF. Trimmed $0.1B vs round 1 because Mobility EBITDA is ~$614M ($5.1B / 8.3x, src 3), implying more exiting FCF than assumed.

389.5M diluted (src 1). The split-off exchange offer (src 13) swaps ETN shares for SpinCo shares. The implied equity value to Eaton holders is ~$4.0B ($5.1B value less the $1.1B cash funded by Mobility debt, src 3). At $432, with a typical exchange-offer discount, that retires ~9-10M shares; I use ~9M. There are no 2026 buybacks (10-Q, src 4).

FY26E FCF of ~$4.0B on a ~$168B market cap is ~2.4% today. I apply 3.1% (round 1: 3.0%) on NTM cash flow, 10bp higher because the 10-year is 5.24% (src 14). Net debt is ~$19.9B at Jun 30 (src 4), falling to ~$17-18B by Sep 2027 from FCF plus the $1.1B RMT cash, less the dividend and COL Group.

bear.story: Hyperscaler capex digests in 2027, or AI financing stress slows data-center orders. The EA margin step-up stalls, and the Fed keeps hiking with the 10-year above 5%. Pro-forma 2027 EPS is ~$14.3 and NTM ~$15.5 at ~19x.

base.story: Backlog converts and price/cost turns into a tailwind. The split-off closes in Q1 2027, retiring ~9M shares; the $1.1B pays down debt. Pro-forma EPS is $15.3 in 2027 and $17.5 in 2028, and the multiple holds ~25-26x NTM despite 5%+ yields.

bull.story: Data-center orders keep compounding (pipeline +130%) and 800V DC and solid-state transformer wins arrive. EA margin heads toward 32% early and rates ease. 2028 PF EPS is ~$18.8 and the stock holds ~31x as a pure-play electrical/aero compounder.

thesis_break_reason: At $330 the stock would sit at ~19.5x pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS of ~$16.95, near the $312 52-week low. With the 10-year above 5%, a de-rating alone could reach the mid-$300s, so $330 on its own is not proof. A break needs confirmation from fundamentals: a negative 12-month rolling order print in Electrical Americas, data-center order cancellations, or a failed H2 segment-margin step-up (Q3 guide 24.6-25.0% vs Q2's 23.1%). If one of those coincides with $330, the thesis is broken.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler/AI data-center capex into 2027-28, the dominant driver (DC orders +85%, pipeline +130% at Laguna).
Rates: 10-year 5.24% and a Fed hiking cycle cap the multiple on a ~27x forward stock.
EA/segment margin step-up in H2 2026. The FY guide was cut to 24.1-24.5% at Q1 (May 5) on Boyd/Ultra PCS consolidation and ramp costs; Q3 needs ~170bp.
Exact RMT dilution: shares retired (exchange ratio and discount), stranded costs, and whether consensus has already removed Mobility.
Leverage (~$19.9B net debt) and no buybacks in 2026.
reasoning: Round 2 keeps my primary-document base: the Q2 release and 10-Q, the RMT 8-K and 425s, and the Laguna remarks. I took the supervisor's fact-checks on board. (1) RMT dilution. I re-derived it from Eaton's own numbers: Mobility segment profit ~$109M/qtr, and a $5.1B value at 8.3x EBITDA from the Jun 11 release, which implies ~$4.0B of equity to Eaton holders and ~9M shares retired. After-tax Mobility profit lost is ~$360M; net of ~$40M interest saved, the dilution is ~$0.5 (~3%), not my round-1 $0.2. Pro-forma 2027 EPS is ~$15.3, 2028 ~$17.5, and NTM at the horizon ~$16.95 (round 1: $17.3). (2) The segment-margin guide cut happened at Q1 (May 5), partly on acquisition mix, not in the Q2 release; I corrected the fact. It does not change the numbers. (3) Rates. FRED confirms the Fed funds upper bound at 4.00% after Sep 17 and the 10-year at 5.24% on Sep 28. I trimmed the P/E to 25.5x and raised the FCF yield to 3.1%. (4) I dropped the X post as a separate source, since it and the investing.com summary report the same Laguna event. P/E gives $432 and FCF yield $424, blending to $430, essentially spot (round 1: $448). Scenarios are $295/$440/$580 at 23/52/25%, mean ~$441, median ~$430. The ladder is a split lognormal with median ~$430, ~35% vol on the downside and ~34% on the upside, set below the 39% realized given backlog visibility and a large-cap base rate of 25-35%. The left tail stays fat for an AI-capex air pocket plus the rate shock. I agree with the supervisor's fair-value direction; my $430 is a bit below its $437 because I apply a small rate haircut to the multiple and retire ~9M rather than ~8M shares (these partly offset). Research was limited to 5 follow-up fetches (EDGAR submissions and RMT filings, FRED).
